implementation_statement: No access control policy existed before 2026. POL-02 (P06), approved 2026-08-31, covers employees, contracted clinicians, agency staff, and vendors. Access procedures are due 2026-11-30.

Employee accounts are created in the identity provider from HR tickets and federated to the EHR; EHR roles come from the vendor role catalog. Contracted clinicians are added by the medical staff office. Gaps: 11 stale accounts for former agency and contracted staff (July 2026); three shared generic accounts; no quarterly access review.
evidence: EV-059 (identity provider export 2026-07-14 reconciled with rosters); EV-004 (HR and agency rosters)

implementation_statement: The EHR enforces role-based access (ED physician, hospitalist, nurse, pharmacist, laboratory, imaging, patient access, business office, HIM). Restricted charts require a logged break-the-glass reason. Cloud tenant access uses provider IAM roles for 2 named administrators.
evidence: EV-006 (EHR role report); EV-016 (cloud IAM export)

implementation_statement: Planned with network segmentation (P01 R-001): firewall rules between user, server, medical device, OT, and phone segments. Today all traffic flows on one network.
Standard users have no local administrator rights. Gaps: MSP technicians share one standing domain administrator account; the analyzer middleware workstation runs as a local administrator.
evidence: EV-013 (directory group export and MSP account list)

implementation_statement: The identity provider locks accounts for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts. The EHR vendor applies the same rule to direct EHR sign-in.
The identity provider and EHR sign-in pages show a notice that access is monitored and limited to authorized users.
Endpoint policy locks screens after 10 minutes. Gap: the ED tracking board and the nursing station shared workstation are exempt.
The EHR ends idle sessions after 15 minutes (vendor setting confirmed).

Employee remote access uses the VPN with identity provider MFA. The EHR vendor, telepharmacy service, and MSP use named accounts. Gap: the teleradiology group's support connection uses a shared VPN account without MFA, active 24x7.

Staff Wi-Fi uses enterprise authentication with directory accounts; guest Wi-Fi is isolated from hospital systems. Infusion pumps use a separate pre-shared-key network that is bridged to the flat network (see SC-7).
Laptops and barcode scanners are enrolled in device management. Gap: clinicians use personal phones for the EHR mobile app without enrollment or app protection.
Awareness and training requirements are in POL-05 (P06), approved 2026-08-31. Procedures for contracted and agency staff are due 2026-11-30.
Annual HIPAA training for employees. Gaps: contracted clinicians and agency nurses are not trained under the hospital program; no security reminders; no phishing exercises.
Planned: downtime and incident roles training for charge nurses, ED staff, and IT (with the 485.625(d) program), starting 2026-11.

provider_if_inherited: EHR vendor; identity provider; cloud provider
implementation_statement: The EHR, identity provider, and cloud tenant log events by default. Gap: firewall, server, EDR, and medical device events are not defined or collected.
evidence: EV-018 (EHR audit documentation); EV-019 (provider audit documentation)

implementation_statement: EHR audit records include user, patient, action, time, and workstation (vendor-defined content).

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Gap: EHR access reports are run only after a complaint, and no other logs are reviewed. Planned: monthly EHR access review focused on staff and well-known patients; weekly identity sign-in review.
evidence: EV-008 (complaint log); EV-062 (Quality and Compliance Manager interview)

implementation_statement: Planned: central log collection with 1-year retention (2027-03-31). Today each system keeps its default (as short as 30 days for some cloud logs).
Audit generation is on for SaaS and cloud services. Gap: the interface engine and imaging archive VMs log locally only.
First control assessment by an independent assessor, 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-07 (P07). Annual cycle each August.
The P07 POA&M tracks every weakness with owner, milestones, and dates; reviewed monthly by the CEO.
Planned: monthly security metrics to the CEO and quarterly to the governing body (open POA&M items, patch status, alerts, access review results).
The MSP maintains a standard workstation image. Gap: no documented baselines for servers, network devices, medical devices, or OT.
Changes to servers and the network are logged in MSP tickets. Gap: no change review for the infusion pump drug library, dispensing cabinets, or OT.
Workstation security settings follow the MSP image. Gap: a manufacturer default password on the patient monitor central station (P07) and default settings on OT controllers.
Unneeded services are removed from the workstation image. Gap: remote access tools on medical device and OT workstations are not reviewed.
IT hardware inventory in the MSP tool. Gap: medical devices tracked only in the biomed maintenance log; OT not inventoried; no MDS2 forms.
The emergency preparedness plan (485.625) is the umbrella. POL-04 and POL-03 add backup and incident duties. An IT contingency plan annex is due 2026-12-31.
Downtime procedures (2019) and two downtime PCs exist. Gap: no IT contingency plan with recovery procedures, roles, and BIA priorities; the emergency plan has no cyber or IT outage annex.
Planned: downtime training for nursing, ED, pharmacy, and laboratory staff with quarterly unit drills.
Planned: quarterly restore tests (first 2026-11-15) and a ransomware and EHR downtime tabletop as the next additional emergency exercise.

The hospital has one campus and no alternate site. The equivalent strategy is patient transfer under agreements with two hospitals (485.625(b)(7)) and the vendor-hosted EHR, which staff can reach from any clean device.
One fiber circuit with a cellular backup on the firewall; analog phone lines in the ED and at the nursing station. Gap: no diverse second carrier; VoIP rides on the flat network.

Nightly backups of on-premises servers to a local appliance with a cloud copy; daily snapshots of cloud workloads. Gaps: the appliance is joined to the directory; the cloud copy is in the production account and region without immutable retention; no backup of OT configurations.
Planned: recovery procedures in BIA priority order in the IT contingency plan (2026-12-31).
Employees and contracted clinicians have unique accounts. Gap: shared accounts on the ED tracking board, analyzer middleware, and nursing station.
Both cloud administrators and the IT Support Specialist use hardware security keys; identity provider administrators require MFA.
MFA for email, remote access, and the cloud console. Gap: on-site EHR sign-in uses a password only; the teleradiology VPN account has no MFA.
Identifiers are unique and assigned by HR or the medical staff office. Gap: identifiers of former agency staff are not disabled on schedule.

The identity provider enforces 14-character passwords and a banned-password list. Gaps: identical local administrator passwords on workstations; a default password on the monitor central station; shared-account passwords never changed.
evidence: EV-002 (identity provider policy); EV-IA-5 (P07 test results)

implementation_statement: POL-03 (P06), approved 2026-08-31. Procedures are in the P08 runbook.
Planned: incident roles training for the CEO, Director of Nursing, charge nurses, and IT before the first tabletop.
Planned: ransomware and EHR downtime tabletop by 2026-11-30, filed as the 485.625(d)(2)(ii) additional exercise.
The MSP handles technical response in business hours; P08 runbook approved 2026-08-31; forensic firm through the cyber insurer's panel. Gap: no 24x7 response; runbook untested.
Planned: security incident category in the ticketing system with an incident log (2026-10-31).
Breach reporting duties are in POL-03 and the P08 matrix. Gap: no published 24x7 reporting line for staff and contracted clinicians.
The P08 runbook covers ransomware with EHR downtime and ambulance diversion. Gap: not yet linked into the emergency plan as an annex.
The biomedical contractor performs preventive maintenance with records in its log. Gap: devices leave for repair without data sanitization and without a BAA.
Vendor remote maintenance for the CT, dispensing cabinets, and OT uses vendor-initiated sessions. Gap: sessions are not approved or logged by IT, and the teleradiology account is shared.
IT drives are destroyed by a certified vendor with certificates. Gap: medical devices with storage are not included.
Badge access is authorized by the department manager and HR; the badge list is reviewed quarterly.
Badge readers on the server room, pharmacy, and ED entrance; main entrance locked at night. Gap: biomedical and OT vendors are not escorted in device and OT areas.
Cameras cover entrances and the server room door. Gap: badge logs are not reviewed.
The generator carries the server room, network, ED, and inpatient unit; tested under NFPA 110 (485.625(e)). The server room also has a UPS.
This SSP, approved 2026-08-31, reviewed annually.
POL-05 rules of behavior approved 2026-08-31. Gap: signed acknowledgments not yet collected from contracted clinicians and agency staff.
The IT Manager is designated Security Officer in writing.
Risk tolerance and acceptance authority are set in POL-01 and P01; the governing body accepts High and Very High risks.
Background checks and license verification for employees; medical staff credentialing for contracted clinicians; agencies attest to screening.
Employee access is disabled within 2 business days of HR notice. Gap: no same-day process; involuntary terminations not handled immediately.
regulatory_driver: C-HPH-R01 (164.308(a)(3)(ii)(C)); C-HPH-R08 (CPG: Revoke Credentials for Departing Workforce Members)

implementation_statement: Agency and group contracts require screening and confidentiality. Gap: agencies do not report assignment end dates; no account expiry.
Handbook discipline applies to employees. Gap: no HIPAA sanctions procedure and none for contracted clinicians. POL-01 4.8 adds it.
HCIS categorized Moderate (section 6 of this SSP); data classified under POL-04.
2026 risk analysis completed (P01) using SP 800-30. Gap: medical device and OT inventory incomplete; prior analysis dated 2023.
Planned: monthly authenticated scanning of servers, workstations, and network devices by the MSP; passive discovery for medical devices (first scan 2026-11-30).
The BIA (P05) identifies critical processes and components and their recovery priority.
EHR and cloud contracts include security terms. Gap: device and OT purchases do not require MDS2, SBOM, or patch support commitments.

BAAs with 8 vendors; EHR vendor SOC 2 reviewed annually (P09). Gaps: no BAA with the cloud fax service or the biomedical contractor; no security review of the MSP, teleradiology, or telepharmacy vendors.
The CT acquisition workstation runs an unsupported operating system; the manufacturer's upgrade path has been requested. Compensating: isolation on a device segment is planned.

A firewall separates the hospital from the internet and terminates VPNs to the EHR vendor and cloud tenant; the imaging archive is reachable only through the VPN. Gap: one flat internal network for users, servers, medical devices, OT, and phones.
TLS for SaaS; IPsec VPN to the cloud tenant and EHR vendor; HL7 over the VPN. Gap: external email containing PHI is not encrypted by default.
Encryption uses provider-managed validated modules for SaaS and cloud storage; laptops use the operating system's full-disk encryption.
Cloud storage and the EHR are encrypted at rest; laptops encrypted. Gap: 88 desktops and workstations on wheels unencrypted.
Monthly OS patching of workstations and servers by the MSP. Gaps: firewall firmware and the infusion pump drug-library server are patched irregularly; medical devices depend on manufacturers.
EDR on servers and workstations. Gaps: alerts watched only in business hours; medical device and OT workstations have no protection.
EDR telemetry and firewall alerts. Gaps: no 24x7 monitoring; no central log correlation; no egress monitoring.
regulatory_driver: C-HPH-R01 (164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D)); C-HPH-R08 (CPG: Detect and Respond to Relevant Threats and Tactics)

implementation_statement: EHR data integrity is vendor-managed. Gap: no integrity monitoring of the infusion pump drug library or dispensing cabinet profiles.
Spam and malicious attachment filtering from the productivity suite; external sender tagging on.
Planned: six-year retention of security documentation in the records schedule (POL-01 4.11).
